_about: V3 rubric for ONE category (format as in v2/rubric). Drafted Nov 18 from the ScholarChain README only; decisions: one rubric with 10 items (user asked for short and sweet); FACTORY-10 and FACTORY-REPLAY-INSUFFICIENT overlap like the README itself (resolve in V4 scoring); FACTORY-02 threshold = refusal + report contract in every agent and at least 5 of the 7 elements. V1 already checks the mechanical half (F, O, R, E, G, W checks); these items judge CONTENT. Per-event deductions that need git history (constitutional change without ratification, reviewer modifying production code, reports claiming commands not run) are left to V1 facts and a human. Nothing in the repository is executed: hooks are judged by reading them.
readme_full_credit: Correct orchestrator and subagent model, one-writer ownership, hooks, permissions, reports, repair loops, human gates, submission of every agent, and exact replay instructions

items.text: Control model. met: CLAUDE.md and docs/agents.md describe the hub-and-spoke model: the main session is the orchestrator, subagents do not call one another and all routing passes through the orchestrator, one fresh orchestrator session per phase, and a blocked agent returns BLOCKED-ON with evidence and the owner, which the orchestrator routes. partial: only some of these are described, or they appear only in a README narrative and not in CLAUDE.md or docs/agents.md.
items.source: 'The reference agentic control model' (control rules 9-12); 'Required factory artifacts': CLAUDE.md, docs/agents.md

items.text: Role files. The seven elements of a subagent file: routing description, narrow tools that fit the role, role statement, non-negotiable laws, ordered procedure, refusal boundaries (declines another owner's artifact and names the correct owner), report contract. met: EVERY agent file has the refusal boundary and the report contract, and at least 5 of the 7 elements. partial: some agents miss the refusal boundary or the report contract, or have fewer than 5 elements. Generic boilerplate repeated unchanged in every agent counts as present but write it in the reason. Open EVERY file under .claude/agents/ before judging this item: a verdict based on a sample of agent files is not acceptable.
items.source: 'Required factory artifacts': .claude/agents/*.md; control rule 2 (decline and name the correct owner)

items.text: Authority separation. met: the required roles exist (a split is fine with non-overlapping ownership; a merge only with a documented instructor approval), AND these four separations are enforced in tool fences or laws: reviewer-class agents have no write tools; test-engineer does not edit production code; infra-engineer may plan but not apply or deploy; deploy-engineer may run approved scripts but not author them. partial: roles missing without explanation, or one to three of the four separations missing.
items.source: 'Agent authority and ownership matrix'; control rules 3, 4, 5, 12

items.text: Ownership map. met: docs/agents.md has a one-writer ownership map that covers the repository's real paths, a lifecycle routing table, authority boundaries, an escalation policy, and human gates; any shared path has documented control. partial: the map exists but misses some of these, or paths in the map do not match the repository layout.
items.source: 'Agent authority and ownership matrix' ('The ownership map in docs/agents.md is authoritative'); 'Required factory artifacts': docs/agents.md

items.text: Hooks enforce the floor (judged by reading the scripts; they are never run). met: guard-dangerous.sh blocks every category the README lists (terraform apply/destroy, force push, reads of .env/secret dirs/private keys/credential files, destructive AWS deletions, recursive S3 deletion, unreviewed EMR termination or large scale-out, edits to ratified constitutional files by non-factory agents) with an actionable message; format-scala.sh exits harmlessly when no Scala file changed; verify-tests-ran.sh compares a test marker with relevant source changes; validate-agent-files.sh checks frontmatter, tool fences, unique names, executable hooks and JSON; settings.json wires them as PreToolUse, PostToolUse and Stop hooks. partial: some hooks are missing these behaviours, or a guard only echoes a warning without blocking.
items.source: 'Required hook and permission behavior'; 'Required factory artifacts': the four hook scripts and settings.json

items.text: MCP policy and commands. met: .mcp.json servers are read-only or narrowly scoped, any write capability is documented with its phase gate, secrets appear only as environment-variable names; the five commands route to their owning agents and state their gates (deploy needs an approved plan and smoke tests; rollback limits autonomous actions; incident routes to incident-responder). partial: some servers have unexplained write capability, or commands route without stating gates.

Phase records. Judge the phases you are given (a sample; V1 checks every phase's consistency with git). met: work orders state concrete inputs, outputs, constraints and acceptance tests; final agent reports exist; reviewer and test-agent reports exist where the phase required them; human gate records state a decision and the accepted commit. partial: work orders are vague (no acceptance tests or no outputs), or required reviewer/test reports are missing.
items.source: 'Agent submission and reproducibility requirements' (work orders, final reports, reviewer and test reports, ratification records, accepted commits); 'Human architect responsibilities' (prompts state inputs, outputs, actors, APIs, constraints, acceptance tests)

items.text: Repair loops and ratification. met: the records show at least one repair handled as the README requires (BLOCKED-ON returned with evidence and owner, routed by the orchestrator, repair validated, blocked agent re-run in a fresh context) and constitutional changes carry human ratification records. partial: some records exist but are incomplete (for example a ratification record but no repair handled as above, or a repair without the re-run). missing: no repair or ratification records; a report or README that only CLAIMS a ratification or repair is not a record. A project with no repair needed is still expected to record ratification of the constitutional files. A human-gate decision that accepts the phase which created or changed the constitutional files counts as a ratification record.
items.source: Control rules 8 and 11; 'Agent submission and reproducibility requirements': human ratification records and repair records

items.text: Agent catalog. met: the README has an agent catalog with one row per submitted subagent giving name, purpose, owned artifact paths, tool fence, prerequisites, an exact example orchestrator instruction (for example 'Use the spark-engineer agent to ...'), the deterministic verification command, and the expected final-report fields. partial: the catalog misses agents or misses some of these columns.
items.source: 'Agent submission and reproducibility requirements': agent catalog paragraph

items.text: Reproduction instructions. met: the README subsection 'Reproducing the agentic workflow' gives the 11 steps in project-specific form (not copied generically), at least one bounded reproduction exercise a grader can run without rebuilding the cloud environment, a version record (Claude Code client version, model configuration when known, JVM, sbt, Scala, Terraform, AWS CLI), and names every external tool, MCP server, permission or environment variable an agent needs with how a grader checks it is available. partial: some of these are missing or the steps are generic.
items.source: 'Agent submission and reproducibility requirements': version record, 'Reproducing the agentic workflow' steps 1-11, bounded reproduction exercise, external requirements

deductions.quote: No independent reviewer or test-agent separation: up to 1.5 points lost. (Judge here: applies when there is no read-only reviewer agent, no test agent separate from implementers, or an agent approves its own work.)

Not all agents used by the project are submitted: up to 2 points lost. (Judge here: applies when phase reports, commands, docs or the agent catalog name an agent that has no file under .claude/agents/.)
Agent invocation and replay instructions are missing or insufficient for a grader to reproduce a bounded phase: up to 2 points lost.
Agents share overlapping write ownership without documented control: up to 1 point lost.

evidence._about: Order matters (capped): constitution, agents, hooks, settings, commands, MCP, README, then phase records (sample: the phases listed in 'phases'). Then every .md under docs/agent-runs/ (reviewer, test, repair and ratification records) until the cap.
